Automate Verse with Make#

Status: the app definition is validated structurally (every module, the connection and the webhook parse and reference the right Verse routes) — it is not yet published to Make's app directory. Until it is, the app is imported into your own Make organisation from integrations/automation/make/ in the repo and invited where it is needed.

A Make scenario can wait for a scene to finish compiling or for a client to pin a comment, then post to Slack, write a sheet row or mail the share link. Going the other way, it can hand Verse a Dropbox or Drive link and get a scene back.

You need: a Verse account token (see Share privately with tokens) and a Make account with the Verse Engine app installed.

1. Connect your account#

When you add the first Verse Engine module, create a connection:

  • Verse server — the origin your account lives on (prefilled with the public host; self-hosters paste their own).
  • Account token — the 64-hex token from POST /v1/account or /studio.

Make tests the connection with GET /v1/account and names it after your account.

2. Modules#

ModuleWhat it does
Instant triggerWatch scene readyRuns when an upload you own finishes or fails: data.job (the scene id), data.url, data.vpkUrl, or data.error + data.code.
Instant triggerWatch review commentsRuns when a reviewer pins a comment: data.scene, data.comment.text, .author, .pos.
ActionUpload a model from a URLHands Verse a public file link (GLB, IFC, USD, FBX/OBJ zip, splat, point cloud); returns job and the share link it will have.
ActionCreate a share linkMints a tokened link for a scene you own — what opens a private scene.
ActionGet scene analyticsViews, unique viewers, time spent, funnel, rooms and daily counts over 7, 30 or 90 days.
SearchList scenesEvery scene you own with its link, visibility, stats and open review count.

Both triggers use one Verse events webhook. When you add the first one, Make asks which events to subscribe to; it registers the hook on your account (POST /v1/account/webhooks) and removes it when you delete the webhook. If one hook carries several events, add a filter on event after the trigger.

3. Worked example: new scene → Slack#

  1. Watch scene ready → Add a webhook, tick Scene ready.
  2. Slack → Create a Message. Text:
    Code
    New scene ready: {{1.data.job}}
{{1.data.url}}
  3. Turn the scenario on. The next upload you own posts its link the moment the compile finishes.

4. Worked example: Dropbox file → Verse scene#

  1. Dropbox → Watch Files on a publish/ folder, then **Dropbox → Get a Link** (direct).
  2. Verse Engine → Upload a model from a URL. File URL: the direct link (dl=1). Scene name: the file name without extension.
  3. The module returns job; the scene is live when Watch scene ready fires for it, or when GET /v1/ingest/<job> says status: done.

Uploads count against your account's ingest rate (20 per hour per token) and the same 512 MB cap as a direct upload; the server fetches the file itself, so the link must be public and direct.

The same thing over HTTP#

Every module is a documented call: subscribe with POST /v1/account/webhooks, upload with POST /v1/ingest/url { "url": "https://…/model.glb", "name": "flat" }, mint a link with POST /v1/scenes/<id>/share. Make's generic HTTP and Webhooks modules can do the same while the app is unlisted.
